items.title: Agencies announce new independent dispute resolution entity, bringing total to 17 - American Hospital Association
items.reason: This item directly reports on CMS/HHS expansion of the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process infrastructure under the No Surprises Act, which is a concrete implementation development affecting revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: Federal agencies have designated a new independent dispute resolution (IDR) entity, bringing the total number of approved IDR entities to 17. This expansion of the IDR network is significant for the No Surprises Act's balance-billing protections, as the IDR process is the mechanism through which out-of-network disputes are resolved when providers and insurers cannot agree on payment amounts. The increase in available IDR entities directly impacts revenue-cycle teams' ability to access the dispute resolution process and influences timelines for resolving payment disagreements on surprise bills.

items.title: Employer, consumer groups urge lawmakers to reform No Surprises Act's IDR - Fierce Healthcare
items.reason: The item directly addresses No Surprises Act implementation and the IDR process, which are core components of the topic, though it focuses on advocacy for reform rather than litigation or regulatory action.
items.summary: Employer and consumer groups have urged lawmakers to reform the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process established under the No Surprises Act, indicating ongoing concerns about the law's implementation mechanisms. The advocacy reflects stakeholder dissatisfaction with how the IDR system is currently functioning to resolve balance-billing disputes between insurers and healthcare providers. This development is relevant to revenue-cycle teams because changes to IDR procedures, timelines, or decision-making criteria could significantly impact claims dispute resolution, payment timelines, and operational costs for managing out-of-network claim disputes.
